Ivy H.: hey all, quick Q for new hires: what channel should i use for small asks vs big requests? and how do i stop bots from filling my feed but still get pings i care about?

Sam (IT): welcome Ivy! quick map: #help = access/laptop/accounts; #people-ops = onboarding/HR stuff; #eng-platform or #eng-infra = infra/training jobs; #random or #lunch-plans = social. For company-wide or outage alerts, use @channel only if it's urgent.

Lena (People Ops): also file PTO/expenses through the apps (don't post receipts in public channels). link to onboarding doc: https://redwood.com/onboarding (has forms and who-to-ask table).

Kai Eng: PR/review etiquette: put links to PRs in #eng-code-reviews, but avoid pasting logs. If you need fast eyes, tag the reviewer in the PR and a short Slack ping.

Ivy H.: bots: i'd like to mute daily standup messages but still get mentions if someone tags me.

Sam (IT): go to channel > Notification preferences > Mentions & reactions and set "All new messages" off, keep "Replies to threads you're in" and "Mentions" on. For very noisy automations, ask channel admins to move them into a dedicated channel like #ci-notifications.

ci-bot: CI: build passed for branch=main commit=abc123 (posted in #ci-notifications)

Kai Eng: reaction norms: use :eyes: for "saw it" and :white_check_mark: for done. saves people from posting many tiny replies.

Lena (People Ops): pro tip: update your Slack timezone and add your manager to #new-hires so they can see your onboarding messages.

Ivy H.: awesome, thanks — i'll post my laptop request in #help and lunch poll in #random. joining #new-hires now :wave:
